title: Last tag
scenario: The tag is the LAST two letters of the code.

intro.job: The tag is the LAST two letters of the code.

idea.rule: Negative indexes count from the end — [-2:] means 'from second-to-last to the finish'.
idea.detail: Seats can be counted from the back too: -1 is the last letter, -2 the one before it. [-2:] starts at seat -2 and, with no stop, runs to the end.

model_restatement: Take the last two letters of the code and print them.

clarify.question: Could a code be shorter than two letters?
Upper or lower case?
clarify.answer: Keep it exactly as it is.

clarify.question: How should I give the tag?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Take two letters of the code for the tag and print it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 1, what is tag?

why_line: code[:2] takes seats 0 and 1 — the FIRST two letters, GO — not the last two.

explain.rule: [:2] counts from the front of the row: seats 0 and 1 are G and O — the wrong end of GOAT.
explain.bridge: So how do you start counting from the back of the row?

fix.rule: [-2:] starts at the second-to-last seat and runs to the end — A, T.

walk.gloss: Start at seat -2 (second from the end) and take the rest.

alternatives.note: The same slice, counted from the front — longer, same answer.

hints: Which letters are at seats 0 and 1?
Negative indexes count from the end.

follow_up.prompt: What does your code give for 'GOL'?
follow_up.fix_hint: The tag is the LAST two letters — with 'GOL', [-2:] gives 'OL', but the draft's [:2] gives the first two, 'GO'.

one_liner: Negative indexes count from the end — [-2:] means 'from second-to-last to the finish'.
